issues.description: The problem statement (Part 1) explicitly asks students to implement a method named `createPerson` on the server side, but the solution's server REST controller implements the POST handler under the name `addPerson`. The template PersonResource is a stub (no method), so students following the textual instruction looking for or implementing `createPerson` may find a mismatch when comparing to the reference solution. This inconsistent naming (createPerson vs addPerson) for the same conceptual operation (POST /persons — create a new Person) can cause unnecessary confusion when students map the written tasks to the server implementation and to the provided solution (especially since the Note endpoints use `createNote` on the server).
issues.suggested_fix: Align the identifier used for the server-side POST handler across artifacts. Either (A) rename the solution's `addPerson` method to `createPerson` to match the problem statement (and keep `createNote` for notes), or (B) update the problem statement to instruct implementing `addPerson` instead of `createPerson`. Apply the same naming convention consistently for similar operations (e.g., use `createX` or `addX` uniformly) to reduce cognitive load.
